tagline: Covered bridges and pioneer graves on the old Darby prairie.
intro: Country roads keep company with Big Darby Creek for more than 27 miles across Union County, by way of Milford Center and Unionville Center. This was the Darby Plains prairie, ground the early settlers thought undesirable because it swung between wet and dry extremes. Some of the prairie survives in pioneer graveyards kept as nature preserves.

Several of the older covered bridges are Reuben Partridge's work. He built more than 200 bridges across Union County and central Ohio, and died in 1900 of complications from a leg broken when he fell through one he was having taken down.
season: The wildflowers in the Bigelow Pioneer Cemetery preserve are at their peak from late July through August.

moments.title: Buck Run Bridge
moments.text: Built in 2006 to replace a steel bridge of 1914, this 160-foot covered span over Big Darby Creek is called the longest single-span wooden bridge in Ohio.

moments.title: Bigelow Pioneer Cemetery
moments.text: Half an acre of graves dug between 1814 and 1892, kept by the state as a nature preserve for one of Ohio's few remaining populations of royal catchfly.

moments.title: Unionville Center
moments.text: The village green was once home to Charles W. Fairbanks, vice president under Theodore Roosevelt, and the village of about 240 holds a festival in his name each May.
